ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Arthur Ashe — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Nine-month HIV review: decision to stop toxoplasmosis maintenance therapy

text.paragraph: Nine-month HIV review: decision about stopping toxoplasmosis maintenance therapy. [S]

Mr. Ashe returns nine months after his first visit, about thirteen months after starting antiretroviral therapy. He has missed no doses and has had no headache, weakness, seizure, rash, fever, or chest pain. His colonoscopy appointment is next month. He has read the result of the syphilis test from the preventive visit, which was sent to him by secure message. He has thought about anal cancer screening and would like to have it at his next visit. Today's blood tests were drawn this morning. [S]

list.item:
Cerebral toxoplasmosis on maintenance therapy (B58.2). All criteria for stopping maintenance are met: six weeks of acute treatment completed, no symptoms, viral load undetectable since three months, and CD4 above 200 for more than six months (218, 262, and now 318). The same counts allow Pneumocystis prophylaxis to stop. [S]
Stop trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole today.
Restart it if the CD4 count falls below 200.
Report any headache, weakness, seizure, or fever the same day.

HIV infection (B20). Viral load not detected for the third time; CD4 318. Blood count normal: hemoglobin 14.1 g/dL, white cells 5.0, platelets 236. Potassium 4.5 mmol/L and creatinine 1.12 mg/dL. [S]
Continue the same regimen.
Viral load and CD4 count in three months, then every three to six months.
Influenza and COVID-19 vaccines today.

Coronary artery disease after two bypass operations (I25.10). No angina; blood pressure at goal. [S]
Yearly lipid panel at the next visit.
